# Learner 01 — Day 080: ML splits, leakage, and baselines

**Personal sequence:** Learner 01, Day 80 of 182. **180 minutes**, including the common architecture huddle, implementation, individual proof, peer review, and breaks. No extra hidden daily hours.

[Full daily coaching guide](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/days/day-080.md) · [Your complete issue sequence](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-01)

## Your implementation goal

**Role:** Workflow and resource lifetime

Implement the ordered workflow for ML splits, leakage, and baselines: input → trusted operation → adapter → result. Connect the agreed collaborators and handle the relevant stop/cleanup/failure path. Delegate display to commands and decisions to core; use the starter scaffold before functions are taught.

**Your exclusive production path:** `src/learnforge/experience/workflows/**`. Edit no other learner's owned production files. Agree shared contracts first with today's integrator, Learner 02. Use the agreed fake to work independently. This is an implementation task; you are not assigned only testing, reviews, or architecture notes.

Build your slice of the same working LearnForge feature. Other learners implement different owned parts; do not implement the whole feature yourself.

## Exact file, unit, and reason

**File:** `src/learnforge/experience/workflows/document_features.py`

**Add or extend:** `run_dataset_split(...)`

**Why this location:** This coordinates ordered steps and resource lifetime: orchestration calls the agreed operations/adapters and handles progress/cleanup without copying their rules.

Reuse the accepted unit where it already exists. Integration/repair days extend it; do not rebuild the same capability. Before coding, the common architecture huddle records the applicable exact signature/types, defaults, valid/invalid results, check order, and allowed mutation from the concrete cases. Early lessons use the supplied module-level scaffold until functions/classes are taught. Future AI/ML feature types are personalized when you choose the track.

## Input, output, and concrete cases

Exact duplicate questions stay in one split; held-out answers are not used to tune thresholds.

Before coding, connect these cases to your own boundary: input shape and units, returned result, invalid-input outcome, and one relevant failure. In a chosen AI/ML track, write equivalent concrete dataset/feature/prediction examples and state the baseline and metric. Keep this an internal working agreement; API documentation remains opt-in.

## Step-by-step explanation: behavior and why

Use this actual example: Exact duplicate questions stay in one split; held-out answers are not used to tune thresholds.

1. **Before:** name the input values, Python types, units, and state before the operation. Predict the observable result.
2. **Checks:** walk the applicable checks in their declared order: representation/shape → local value bounds → trusted identity/scope → business state. Skip checks that do not belong to this unit and explain their actual owner. Reject invalid input before an unauthorized or partial effect.
3. **Mechanism:** trace the calculation, branch, lookup, iteration, await, model/retrieval step, or transition using actual intermediate values. Explain the Python/library/system rule that causes each change; do not just narrate line names.
4. **After:** show the returned/displayed value and any permitted state change. Compare the observed outcome with the stated expectation. Name what remains unchanged.
5. **Failure variation:** change one relevant input or interrupt a dependency. Trace the different path, error, cleanup, cancellation, or recovery and explain why it behaves differently.

The walkthrough explains implementation behavior; it is not an undisclosed extra feature or test-authoring requirement. Use the learner's actual file/line and revision during review. If the learner asks for a fuller explanation, break the mechanism into smaller steps and examples.

## Scope and progressive research hints

Implement only today's named owned slice and the agreed observable behavior. Adjacent roadmap features, broad abstractions, speculative optimization, other learners' modules, API documentation, and large test suites are outside this increment unless explicitly added to the task. A review cannot silently turn a learning question into new feature work.

1. Search the exact Python/framework/model term from today's guide and read the smallest relevant official example.
2. Compare the chosen approach with one simpler alternative at today's boundary; identify what each guarantees.
3. Diagnose one question: which input, state change, or dependency outcome makes this observed result happen, and why? Use actual values before changing code.

## One architecture topic — all six together

**Define a cheap baseline and success measure before buying a model or building a complex pipeline.**

Attend the same project-level discussion as the other five learners. Compare options, agree one decision, then implement its effect in your owned slice. Facilitator: Learner 02. Record one shared decision, not six separate architectures. You must personally explain the invariant, failure, and trade-off.

## Your concept proof and Question of the Day

Create a small independent proof in `practice/learner-01/day-080/` using today's concept, including the part implemented by another role. Predict one normal output and one fresh changed case before running it. Use your own values; do not copy a peer's answer. Read the full guide for the short concept explanation, pitfalls, two-question quiz, coding drill, and coach-key link.

**Question of the Day (retention from Day 059):** Why is a globally valid ID not permission to read its record?

Explain an example, then answer a changed assumption. In the final stage also explain the data, relevant mathematics, baseline, and failure case of your chosen AI/ML topic. Individual weak areas receive a small targeted repair recorded in your ledger; a peer's pass does not replace yours.

## Your peer-review responsibility

Review **Learner 06's Day 080 implementation**. Their sequence is in the [issue index](https://github.com/Prem-Tomar/python-fastapi-genai-agents-coaching/blob/main/ISSUES.md#learner-06). The rotation covers every other learner over five days. Review behavior and the agreed architecture first, then clarity and one relevant edge case. Explain the concept behind a finding; the owner makes the fix. Respond to the peer reviewing your work.

## Light checking and visible integration

Run a small behavior example plus existing relevant checks. Learn or revisit one short testing pattern when relevant; no testing-only task, dedicated tester, coverage quota, or large test suite. Demonstrate your slice connected to the working product, with honest partial/failure outcomes. Keep the last working flow available.

- [ ] Its relevant normal/failure examples work in the integrated product.
